Because technically you need to make a new version to submit. You can end the version as soon as it start to make it a unsuccessful one, yet you still need at least some free gpu quota to make it actually start. It's just how code competition works on kaggle.

You can still submit those old version you made before if it's a successful one, since they already have a output file.

Another option it's to subscribe Colab pro, it will give you extra 15 hour GPU quota. It's very cheap on taobao.

I found it: the Colab link is broken on Kaggle:

Remove the broken link: On your Kaggle settings page, scroll down to the Google connection option and click Unlink. Re-establish the link properly: Open any Kaggle notebook. In the top menu, click File > Link to Colab. A Google pop-up window will open: carefully select the email address associated with your Colab Pro subscription.

That's it!

For anyone who might find this helpful...
